newsitem.title: UK: BAA still confident of avoiding windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: BAA still confident of avoiding windfall tax.

text.p: British airports operator BAA Plc said on Firday it was confident it would not be hit by the opposition Labour Party's proposed windfall tax, despite a new report that said it had new evidence that BAA would be liable.

BAA's share price fell on Friday after the Financial Times newspaper said it had obtained details of Labour's plans, which indicated BAA would be liable along with any other "privatised utilities whose business is licensed and regulated by statute."
"We don't believe it will apply to us," corporate affairs director Des Wilson said when asked to comment on the report.

"We have not had a windfall, we have not made excess profits, we are not a utility. We have increased employment and spent hugely on infrastructure and therefore it would be completely unreasonable and we cannot believe that they (Labour) would take such a step," he said.

Labour originally said it would impose the tax on firms which it had accused the Conservative government of selling off too cheaply, allowing "fat cat" managers and shareholders to benefit at the expense of taxpayers and customers.

But speculation has been growing that Labour now wants to cast a wider net over the privatised sector in order to raise up to 10 billion stg and to avoid any accusations of discriminating against a particular industry or sector.
By 1130 GMT BAA's share price was down 12-1/2p at 532-1/2 in a generally firmer market.
